Package hadur117.core.move

Class HitForensics

java.lang.Object
hadur117.core.move.HitForensics
public final class HitForensics extends Object
MOVE-9: why an enemy bullet that hit us got through, for the HF record (plan-top3 stage 0, docs/plan-top3.md). Measurement only: nothing here changes where we drive.

A hit is classed by the guess factor it came from. headon when it lies within our half-width of guess factor 0, linear when it lies within our half-width of where a linear gun would have aimed from our lateral velocity at fire time, learned otherwise; nowave when no firing wave carried it. The danger percentile says how the surf's own views rated the angle the bullet came from: the share of the wave's guess factors in [-1, 1] that they scored less dangerous. Near 0 the views thought the angle safe (a learning miss); near 1 they knew it was dangerous (a reach or choice miss).

Angles are radians and guess factors on the classic scale (Wave#guessFactor). The class is stateless.

    • record

      public static String record(int round, long tick, String cls, double gf, double linearGf, double dangerPct, double distance, double power, boolean driving, double planOffset, double planDanger, long planAge, String options, long optionsAge)
      The HF record: HF,round,tick,class,gf,linearGf,dangerPct,distance,power,driving, planOffset,planDanger,planAge,options,optionsAge, NaN (or -1 for the age) for what a hit cannot know. The plan fields read the surf's last plan on the hit's wave: how far off it the hit was (planOffset(hadur117.core.move.PlanInterval, double)), the danger the surf gave it, and how many ticks before the hit it was published. options is optionFlags(hadur117.core.move.PlanInterval[], int, double) on the wave's first options, published optionsAge ticks before the hit (MOVE-10).
